strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing asymmetric alignment between single visual and hierarchical textual features with clear problem formulation
Solid heterogeneous manifold alignment algorithm with theoretical guarantees (existence and uniqueness of optimal intermediate manifold)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across four datasets, multiple protocols (few-shot, base-to-base/novel/whole), and three complementary metrics
Consistent improvements across settings, especially on HCA metric (up to 28.83% improvement in 16-shot, 41.17% vs HyCoCLIP)
Effective visualizations (attention maps, t-SNE) and thorough ablation studies validating each component
Strong reproducibility efforts with detailed implementation, complete proofs, and commitment to open-source release
weaknesses: Limited novelty of individual components (intermediate layers, cross-attention, hyperbolic embeddings all established); main contribution (heterogeneous curvatures) is incremental

Theoretical contributions somewhat expected: Theorem 1 relies on Taylor approximation without discussing approximation error bounds or validity conditions; Propositions 1-2 provide intuitive but not surprising guarantees
Key hyperparameter choices lack justification: Why layers 4 and 7? No ablation on layer selection; k=0.1 in cone formula fixed without sensitivity analysis; α=0.5 for entailment loss not validated

Missing statistical rigor: results averaged over only 3 runs with no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; modest improvements in some settings (1-3%) don't clearly justify added complexity

Insufficient experimental scope: limited baseline comparisons, evaluation restricted to hierarchical classification, unclear applicability to other hierarchical VLM tasks (retrieval, detection, segmentation)
External hierarchy dependency not addressed: for CIFAR-100/SUN/ImageNet, hierarchies constructed from WordNet may not reflect actual image distributions; Rare Species performance notably weaker

Method complexity insufficiently justified: combines many components (intermediate layers, cross-attention, dual hyperbolic spaces, intermediate manifold search via golden section + implicit differentiation, entailment constraints); computational overhead vs baselines not reported

Design decisions lack validation: motivation for intermediate manifold alignment versus direct alignment unclear; cross-attention mechanism is standard without comparing alternatives; entailment constraints not validated as optimal for hierarchical relationships

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 datasets and multiple settings with strong empirical results (up to 28.83% HCA improvement)
Detailed ablation studies demonstrating contribution of each component
Theoretical framework with existence and uniqueness proofs for intermediate manifold
Good visualizations (attention maps, t-SNE) supporting the approach
Thorough reproducibility details in appendices

Questionable design choices: disabling cross-token self-attention poorly justified; hyperparameters (α=0.5, layers 4&7) lack ablation; asymmetric entailment assumption not validated

Experimental limitations: only 2 hyperbolic baselines compared, missing recent hierarchical alignment methods, no statistical significance testing, results averaged over just 3 runs, method built on MaPLe/PromptSRC making comparisons potentially unfair
Task-specific design with unclear generalization: method explicitly for hierarchical/taxonomic classification; tested only on image classification; no exploration of other VLM alignment problems

Inconsistent ablation results: HypV2 achieves 51.67 HCA vs. full method 53.19 (1.52 point gain) on Cifar100 1-shot—unclear if added complexity of Theorem 1, Propositions 1-2, and implicit differentiation is justified
Rare Species is newly proposed benchmark without community validation
Missing analysis of computational costs and training time
Concept of 'symmetric alignment' mentioned but never formally defined or measured

strengths: Well-motivated problem: clearly articulates the asymmetry in existing methods and proposes an intuitive hierarchical alignment solution
Solid theoretical contributions: Theorems 1-2 and Propositions 1-2 provide formal guarantees for intermediate manifold construction, even if based on approximations
Comprehensive experimental validation: extensive experiments across 4 datasets, 3 metrics, multiple settings with consistent improvements and thorough ablations
Strong technical execution: semantic-aware feature extraction framework is well-designed; use of learnable curvatures per modality is sensible
Excellent reproducibility: complete proofs, implementation details, hyperparameters, and visualizations; commitment to open-source release
Effective qualitative analysis: GradCAM visualizations convincingly demonstrate hierarchical attention patterns align with taxonomic levels
weaknesses: Theoretical approximations weaken guarantees: Taylor expansion introduces 5.3% mean error; distance measure D_L is not a formal metric (asymmetric, violates triangle inequality); constant r estimation is ad-hoc
Limited component-level novelty: intermediate layers, hyperbolic embeddings, and cross-attention are all established techniques; the contribution is primarily in their combination
Narrow scope: method is specialized for hierarchical/taxonomic data; applicability to standard vision-language tasks without hierarchies is unclear and unexplored

Mixed experimental results: performance gains vary significantly by dataset—strongest on naturally hierarchical data (CIFAR100, Rare Species) but weaker on artificial hierarchies (ImageNet, SUN); base-to-novel generalization shows inconsistent transfer

Methodological concerns: cross-token attention suppression lacks strong empirical grounding; layer selection (4,7,11) justification via Information Bottleneck is hand-wavy; claimed 'symmetric alignment' still enforces asymmetric entailment constraints
Incomplete comparisons: missing direct comparisons with hierarchical VLM methods (BioCLIP, BioCLIP2); only two hyperbolic baselines; no comparisons with other intermediate-layer fusion approaches
Presentation issues: paper is dense with heavy notation; frequent appendix references make standalone reading difficult; complexity may limit accessibility
Practical overhead: ~30% training time increase and multiple hyperparameters add complexity for prompt-tuning applications; sensitivity to hierarchy quality/definition not thoroughly analyzed

strengths: Well-motivated problem of symmetric vs asymmetric modality alignment with clear intuition
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple datasets, settings, metrics, and detailed ablations
Strong empirical results showing consistent improvements (up to 28.83% HCA) across benchmarks
Thorough reproducibility appendices with implementation details and proofs
Addresses an underexplored task (taxonomic open-set classification) systematically
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: heterogeneous curvatures—the main contribution—provide only marginal improvement (~1-2%) over shared curvature baseline, with 30% training overhead

Theoretical concerns: Distance metric DL explicitly not a formal metric; involves multiple approximations (Taylor expansion with max error 32.4%, constant r estimation, numerically-derived y₁*) without rigorous justification
Narrow evaluation scope: almost exclusively on taxonomic classification (one task type); no evaluation on standard VLM benchmarks (ImageNet zero-shot, COCO retrieval); no true cross-domain evaluation
Suspicious baseline gaps: 25.89% LA improvement over HyCoCLIP in Table 4 suggests possible baseline implementation issues
Semantic-aware feature extraction lacks novelty: straightforward combination of known ideas; ablation (Table 9) shows cross-attention suppression causes minimal performance drop (0.42%)
Class imbalance not addressed: Appendix C.12 only applies sample re-weighting; inherent robustness to hierarchical imbalance unclear
Statistical significance not reported: Results averaged over 3 runs with no error bars or confidence intervals; critical for marginal improvements at 30% acceptance rate
Reproducibility: Code unavailable despite reproducibility claims; some architectural details remain unclear

strengths: Novel heterogeneous manifold alignment algorithm with learnable modality-specific curvatures and optimized intermediate manifold
Semantic-aware visual feature extraction with text-guided cross-attention effectively constructs hierarchical features
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets, settings, and metrics with substantial improvements (up to 28.83% HCA, 25.89% LA vs. baselines)
Thorough ablation studies validating each component and design choice
Excellent reproducibility with detailed implementations, hyperparameters, and commitment to open-sourcing
Strong visualizations (t-SNE, GradCAM) demonstrating meaningful hierarchical semantic learning
Theoretical contributions with proofs of existence and uniqueness for optimal intermediate manifold
weaknesses: Distance measure D_L lacks formal metric properties (asymmetric, violates triangle inequality) and relies on Taylor approximation with 5.3% mean error
Evaluation limited to taxonomic classification—generalizability to other hierarchical tasks unclear; narrow scope limits impact
No statistical significance testing despite averaging over only 3 runs; cannot confirm statistical significance of improvements
Semantic-aware feature extraction partially incremental—using intermediate layers is established; main novelty is cross-attention suppression which shows modest isolated gains (Table 9)
Hyperparameter choices somewhat arbitrary: layer selection [4,7,11] lacks deep justification despite robustness claims; multiple hyperparameters (α, learning rates, initialization) require tuning
Missing failure case analysis and discussion of task conditions where method struggles; all results show improvements warranting critical analysis
Rare Species data preprocessing ad-hoc (concatenating taxonomic levels); alternative representation significantly degrades performance, raising concerns about robustness
~30% training time overhead despite 'negligible cost' claims; computational burden could be significant for large-scale applications
Class imbalance handling relegated to appendix as afterthought; method not inherently robust to imbalance
Theoretical contributions rely on approximations: r estimated per-batch with unclear theoretical implications; wrapped normal distribution choice not justified
